title: Open problem on quantum ergodicity over small spectral windows (Remark 1.2)
statement_text: It would be interesting to see whether the authors' examples (sequences of $(d+1)$-regular expanders on $m$ vertices with high girth having $\alpha\log_d(m)$ eigenvalues in $(-2\sqrt{d},2\sqrt{d})$ of multiplicity $\Omega(m^{1-4\alpha})$, each eigenspace having an orthogonal basis of eigenvectors supported on sets of size $O(m^{\alpha})$) can prove a lower bound on the length of the smallest spectral window $I\subset(-2\sqrt{d},2\sqrt{d})$ for which quantum ergodicity over $I$ holds; the problem of controlling the other eigenvectors in such a window well enough to say that the quantum-ergodicity average in a small window of width roughly $1/\log(m)$ is not equidistributed is not pursued and remains open.
context_text: Let $G_m$ be a sequence of $(d+1)$-regular graphs on $m$ vertices with adjacency matrices $A_m$ and an orthonormal eigenbasis $\psi^{(m)}_1,\dots,\psi^{(m)}_m$. Anantharaman and Le Masson (see also Brooks, Le Masson and Lindenstrauss) proved quantum ergodicity on graphs: if $G_m$ converges to the tree in the Benjamini–Schramm sense (e.g. girth tending to infinity) and has a uniform spectral gap ($|\lambda_i(A_m)|<(d+1)(1-\beta)$ for all nontrivial eigenvalues), then for every sequence of test functions $a_m:V_m\to\mathbb{R}$ with $\sum_x a_m(x)=0$ and $\|a_m\|_\infty\le1$, the average $\frac1m\sum_{i\le m}|\langle\psi^{(m)}_i,a_m\psi^{(m)}_i\rangle|^2$ tends to $0$, i.e. eigenvectors are equidistributed on average; a refined version takes this average only over the eigenvectors whose eigenvalues lie in a spectral window $I\subset(-2\sqrt d,2\sqrt d)$, and holds for windows of width roughly $1/\log(m)$. For every prime $p$ with $d=p+1$ and $\alpha\in(0,1/6)$, the authors construct explicit $(d+1)$-regular graphs with all nontrivial eigenvalues at most $(3/\sqrt2)\sqrt d$ in absolute value, girth at least about $2\alpha\log_d(m)$, and many eigenvectors with eigenvalues in $(-2\sqrt d,2\sqrt d)$ supported entirely on a set of size $O(m^\alpha)$ (a discrete analogue of scarring), showing that these hypotheses do not imply quantum unique ergodicity; a variant yields many localized eigenvectors of very high multiplicity in a very small spectral window.
notes: Stated in prose inside Remark 1.2, not a labelled theorem environment. PDF source — surrounding math may be partially garbled.
paper_title: High-girth near-Ramanujan graphs with localized eigenvectors
